# Writing Safe C in 2026

C is not going away. Here's how to write it safely.

## Use `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`

Treat every warning as an error from day one. Retrofitting this onto an existing codebase is painful.

## Prefer stack allocation

Every `malloc` is a liability. If it fits on the stack, put it there.

## Use AddressSanitizer in CI

Add `-fsanitize=address` to your CI build. It catches buffer overflows and use-after-free at runtime.

## Static analysis

`clang-tidy` and `cppcheck` catch patterns the compiler misses. Run them on every pull request.
